issues.legal_issue: A plea of res judicata that depends on factual determinations cannot be directed to be tried as a preliminary issue in a civil suit.
material_facts: The plaintiffs brought a civil suit seeking declarations concerning ownership and an earlier decree, as well as a permanent injunction.
The defendant sought to have res judicata tried as a preliminary issue; the trial court refused, and the High Court directed it to frame that preliminary issue.
The res judicata plea depended on the pleadings, parties, and proceedings in the earlier suit and was a mixed question of law and fact.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s direction was set aside. The trial court must record findings on all issues rather than try the mixed res judicata issue as a preliminary issue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XIV Rule 2(1) and (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court ordinarily must pronounce judgment on all issues. It may try an issue first only where the issue is one of law alone and concerns the court’s jurisdiction or a legal bar to the suit; even then, doing so is discretionary. A mixed issue of law and fact, or an issue of law that depends on facts, cannot be tried as a preliminary issue. Order XX Rule 5 and Order XLI Rules 24 and 25 support recording findings on all issues to facilitate appellate determination and avoid remand. Major S.S. Khanna v. Brig. F.J. Dillon and Ramesh B. Desai v. Bipin Vadilal Mehta establish that mixed issues cannot be tried preliminarily; Jamia Masjid v. K.V. Rudrappa recognizes that res judicata may be decided preliminarily where no disputed factual or mixed question requires determination. The Court also considered Abdul Rahman v. Prasony Bai and Srihari Hanumandas Totala v. Hemant Vithal Kamat. The procedural purpose of these rules is to advance justice and promote expeditious, final resolution of litigation, as reflected in Sardar Amarjit Singh Kalra v. Pramod Gupta, Kailash v. Nanhku, Sugandhi v. P. Rajkumar, and A. Shanmugam v. Ariya Kshatriya Rajakula Vamsathu Madalaya Nandhavana Paripalanai Sangam.

predicates.civil_suit: A claimant filed a civil suit for adjudication of a dispute.
predicates.defendant_seeks_preliminary_issue: The defendant asked the court to decide an issue before trying the other issues in the suit.
predicates.res_judicata_plea_requires_examination_o: Resolving the plea requires examining facts about the parties, pleadings, or decision in an earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks early determination in a civil suit of a res judicata plea that requires examination of facts about an earlier suit, the trial court must decide all issues together.
